drafts.subject: launch day is day one, not the finish line
drafts.text:
Hi Product Hunt team,

makers ship on launch day, then go quiet. the buyers are already typing the question somewhere else.

Viewfy finds those threads, drafts the reply in the maker's voice, and waits for approval. we'd love to give every PH maker their first post free, or write a guide on the 30 days after launch.

Viewfy, the growth agent that gets you users while you ship.
find 5 threads from this week where someone asks for exactly what you built. answer them properly, no link unless they ask. the buyers are already typing the question.
The build is just the empty box. Marketing fills it. You guys built a real calendar, not a demo. That's the hard part. Launch is easy. Getting people to care is the work. Congrats.
Marketing isn't a department you hire later, it's every commit you make. The post you draft today is the first draft of your product. And the next one comes tomorrow.

The marketing team doesn't suck. They were always 20 tasks behind. You build the product, they queue up marketing, and the queue gets 3 months deep before the first post exists. So marketing has always been the hard part.
First 3 users define your ICP, not a page. Get one to interview you for 20 mins, record it, extract the customer profile together. Sell before the landing page exists. Market later.
same. what worked for me: write down where your buyers ask the question (reddit, X, HN), check it every morning, answer 3 threads. boring, repeatable, and it doesn't reset per project.

4-6 apps isn't competition. It means the market exists. The guy on your competitor's list who never signed up? That's not a rival. That's your first customer. They're just waiting for a thread to catch them.
just ship it to one person who needs it. doesn't need to be viral. a paying customer is better feedback than 100 free signups who leave.
the old playbook was rank and wait. now buyers ask ChatGPT and Reddit instead. go answer them there, in the thread, while it's still alive. distribution didn't die, it moved.
10 years of shipping is the hard part. marketing is just a second product you haven't built yet. same loop: talk to users, ship small, keep what worked. you'll get good at this one faster.

first user comes from one place: a person you talked to today about something useful.

x replies, blog posts, cold email all fill the gaps. a human in the thread gets the first one.

who's on your list?

Congrats on the first customers! That's the real milestone. Handling a few users yourself is totally fair. When the onboarding alone takes 4 hours a week, then you'll know it's time to hire. Don't rush it.

You're already doing the hard part: shipping. Most founders spend weeks on landing pages and never turn the server on. Your product did the marketing by helping someone actually grow. That's the real case study.
This is the real gap. product is the floor, distribution is the ceiling. most founders pour all the energy into the floor and wonder why traffic never reaches the ceiling.
8 years of showing up every day. that's the whole game, not the launch. congrats man 🤟
Shipped hourly outcome tracking this week. Every reply we draft gets scored an hour later: replied, liked, booked a call. The next draft learns from it. You still approve before anything posts. 💙
Generic AI sounds generic. Viewfy now drafts in your voice, trained on your own posts and emails. The best edit is the one you don't have to make.

Profound just raised $180M on AI visibility. Meanwhile 27% of the Show HN launches we scanned can't be read by AI engines at all. Start with access. Viewfy checks it and opens the fix as a pull request.
